q: Which address ranges should a VNet normally use?
exp: Use private ranges that don't overlap with networks you'll connect to.

q: Which CLI command creates a VNet with one subnet?
opts: az network vnet create -g RG1 -n VNet1 --address-prefix 10.0.0.0/16 --subnet-name Web --subnet-prefix 10.0.1.0/24
exp: az network vnet create can create the first subnet inline.

q: Which CLI command adds a subnet to an existing VNet?
opts: az network vnet subnet create -g RG1 --vnet-name VNet1 -n App --address-prefixes 10.0.2.0/24
exp: Subnets are child resources of the VNet.

q: What's the smallest subnet size Azure allows for IPv4?
exp: /29 is the smallest: 8 addresses with 3 usable.

q: Can you change a subnet's address range while VMs are deployed in it?
opts: Only if the new range still contains all the existing IP addresses in use; otherwise remove the resources first
exp: Subnet changes must keep existing IP allocations valid.

q: What's the minimum recommended size for GatewaySubnet?
exp: Microsoft recommends /27 or larger for GatewaySubnet.

q: A subnet is delegated to Microsoft.Web/serverFarms. What does that mean?
opts: The subnet is dedicated to that service (here, App Service VNet integration), which can create service-specific resources in it
exp: Subnet delegation lets a PaaS service inject resources into the subnet.

q: VMs in VNet1 need a custom DNS server (10.0.0.10, a domain controller). Where do you set it?
exp: DNS servers are set at the VNet level (a NIC can override); VMs pick them up via DHCP after a restart or lease renewal.

q: VMs aren't picking up a newly configured custom DNS server on the VNet. What should you do?
opts: Restart the VMs (or renew DHCP leases) so they receive the new DNS settings
exp: DNS changes are applied through DHCP.

q: A domain controller VM needs a private IP that never changes. Configure:
opts: Static private IP allocation on the NIC
exp: Set the NIC IP configuration to Static in Azure. Don't set static IPs inside the guest OS.

q: Why shouldn't you configure a static IP manually inside a Windows VM's network adapter settings?
opts: It can cause loss of connectivity if it doesn't match Azure's assignment; configure the IP on the Azure NIC instead
exp: Azure assigns IPs via DHCP; mismatched in-guest settings break connectivity.

q: Which CLI command creates a static Standard public IP?
opts: az network public-ip create -g RG1 -n pip1 --sku Standard --allocation-method Static
exp: Specify the Standard SKU and static allocation.

q: A Standard public IP should survive a full zone failure. Which option?
exp: Zone-redundant IPs are served from all zones.

q: You need a contiguous range of static public IPs for allowlisting with a partner. Which resource?
exp: A public IP prefix reserves a contiguous block of addresses.

q: Many VMs without public IPs need outbound internet access from a few predictable public IPs. Best service?
opts: NAT Gateway associated with the subnet
exp: NAT Gateway provides scalable outbound SNAT from static IPs or prefixes.

q: A subnet has a NAT Gateway, and a VM in it also has an instance-level public IP. Which IP does the VM's outbound traffic use?
opts: The NAT Gateway's public IP (NAT Gateway takes precedence for outbound)
exp: NAT Gateway takes precedence over other outbound methods, including instance-level public IPs and load balancer outbound rules. The VM's public IP is still used for inbound traffic.

q: Microsoft has been retiring default outbound access for VMs. What's the recommended explicit outbound method?
opts: NAT Gateway (or a load balancer outbound rule, or an instance public IP)
Rely on implicit default outbound IPs
exp: Use explicit outbound methods; new subnets can be created as private subnets.

q: Which CLI command creates one side of a peering from VNet1 to VNet2?
opts: az network vnet peering create -g RG1 -n v1-to-v2 --vnet-name VNet1 --remote-vnet VNet2 --allow-vnet-access
exp: You create peering on each side (or use the portal, which can create both).

q: Peering shows 'Initiated' on VNet1 and doesn't exist on VNet2. What's wrong?
opts: The peering hasn't been created on VNet2 yet; both sides must be configured to reach 'Connected'
exp: Peering needs links on both VNets.

q: After adding a new address prefix to VNet1, peered VNet2 can't reach the new range. What should you do?
opts: Sync the peering (resync the remote address space) on the peering link
exp: After an address-space change, sync the peering to update the remote side.

q: An NVA in the hub forwards traffic from Spoke1 to Spoke2. Which peering setting must allow traffic that didn't originate in the peered VNet?
exp: Forwarded traffic covers traffic routed through an NVA.

q: How is VNet peering billed?
opts: Per GB of ingress and egress traffic across the peering (higher for global)
exp: Peering charges for data transfer in both directions.

q: Answer Yes or No:
stmts: VNets in different Entra tenants can be peered
Peering is supported between VNets in different regions
Overlapping address spaces can be peered if you use NAT
exp: Cross-tenant and global peering are supported; no gateway is needed; overlapping spaces can't peer.

q: Which service connects an on-premises network to an Azure VNet over an encrypted IPsec tunnel across the internet?
opts: Site-to-site VPN through a VPN gateway
exp: Site-to-site VPN uses IPsec/IKE over the internet.

q: Which resource represents your on-premises VPN device and address ranges in Azure?
exp: The local network gateway holds the on-premises public IP and prefixes.

q: Order the steps to create a site-to-site VPN:
items: Create the connection with a shared key
Create GatewaySubnet and the virtual network gateway
exp: Gateway → local network gateway → connection → configure the on-prem device.

q: Individual remote users' laptops need a VPN to the Azure VNet. Which option?
exp: Point-to-site connects individual clients.

q: Which connectivity option gives a private, dedicated connection to Azure that doesn't go over the public internet?
exp: ExpressRoute uses a connectivity provider's private circuit.

q: Deploying a new VPN gateway takes a long time. Typically how long?
opts: Up to about 45 minutes or more
exp: Gateway creation commonly takes 30–45+ minutes.

q: Without any UDRs, how does Azure route traffic between subnets in the same VNet?
opts: It doesn't — you must add routes
exp: System routes cover intra-VNet traffic.

q: Which CLI commands create a route table and a route to an NVA?
opts: az network route-table create ... then az network route-table route create --next-hop-type VirtualAppliance --next-hop-ip-address 10.0.100.4
exp: Create the table, add routes, then associate it with subnets.

q: You created a route table with a UDR, but traffic doesn't follow it. What's commonly missing?
opts: Associating the route table with the subnet
exp: Route tables apply only when associated with subnets.

q: Routes for 10.0.0.0/16 (→ VNet) and 10.0.5.0/24 (→ NVA) both exist. Where does traffic to 10.0.5.20 go?
opts: To the NVA — longest prefix match wins
exp: The most specific prefix (/24) wins.

q: Which route table setting stops on-premises BGP routes from the VPN gateway from being added to a subnet?
opts: Propagate gateway routes = No (disable BGP route propagation)
exp: Disabling gateway route propagation keeps BGP routes out.

q: Traffic arrives at an NVA VM but isn't forwarded on. What's commonly missing?
opts: IP forwarding on the NVA's NIC in Azure, plus forwarding enabled inside the OS
exp: Both the Azure NIC setting and OS-level forwarding are required.

q: Which TWO are valid UDR next-hop types?
exp: Next hops: Virtual appliance, Virtual network gateway, Virtual network, Internet, None.

q: With 0.0.0.0/0 → NVA on a subnet, VMs still reach Azure Storage directly through a service endpoint. Why?
opts: Service endpoint routes are more specific system routes that apply for the service's prefixes
exp: Service endpoints add optimized routes for service prefixes, which bypass the default route.

q: Answer Yes or No:
stmts: One route table can be associated with multiple subnets
A UDR can override the system route for VNet-local traffic
Effective routes can be viewed per NIC
exp: Route tables can be shared; UDRs can override VNet routes; system routes can't be deleted, only overridden; effective routes are per NIC.

q: Two VMs in peered VNets can ping by IP but not by hostname. What's the cause?
opts: Azure-provided DNS doesn't resolve names across VNets; use a private DNS zone linked to both VNets or a custom DNS server
exp: Cross-VNet name resolution needs private DNS or a custom DNS server.

q: Which Network Watcher tool shows whether VM1 can reach an FQDN on port 443 right now, including latency and the hops?
exp: Connection troubleshoot tests connectivity from a VM to a destination at a point in time.

q: Ping (ICMP) between two Windows VMs fails, but RDP between them works. What's the likely cause?
opts: The Windows Firewall inside the guest blocks ICMP by default
exp: The guest OS firewall often blocks ICMP.

q: You can't RDP to a VM. Which first checks are correct?
opts: NSG rules (effective security rules), VM running state, public IP/Bastion path, and the guest firewall
exp: Check the network path, the NSGs, and the VM state.

q: Which feature isolates a whole subnet from internet outbound access by default for new deployments?
exp: Private subnets disable default outbound access, so outbound must be explicit.

q: Which service centrally manages connectivity configurations (hub-spoke, mesh) and security admin rules across many VNets?
exp: Virtual Network Manager handles connectivity and security admin rules at scale.

q: Can a VNet span multiple subscriptions?
opts: No — a VNet belongs to one subscription; use peering to connect VNets across subscriptions
exp: Each VNet lives in one subscription.

q: Can you move a VM's NIC to a different VNet?
opts: No — a NIC's VNet can't change; create a new NIC in the target VNet (or recreate the VM)
exp: A NIC is bound to its VNet; you can only change subnets within the same VNet.

q: Can a VM's NIC move to a different subnet in the SAME VNet?
opts: Yes — change the subnet in the NIC's IP configuration (static IPs must be updated)
exp: Subnet changes within the same VNet are supported.

q: VNet1 in West Europe must connect to VNet2 in East US with an encrypted tunnel through gateways (not peering). Which option?
exp: VNet-to-VNet uses VPN gateways with IPsec.

q: Can a VM NIC have multiple IP configurations?
opts: Yes — a NIC can have multiple private IPs (and associated public IPs)
exp: NICs support secondary IP configurations.

ctx: VNet-Hub (10.0.0.0/16) has GatewaySubnet and a VPN gateway. VNet-Spoke (10.1.0.0/16) is peered with 'Use remote gateways'. On-premises is 192.168.0.0/16.
q: Answer Yes or No:
stmts: VNet-Spoke VMs can reach on-premises through the hub gateway
VNet-Spoke can also deploy its own VPN gateway while using remote gateways
Hub peering must have 'Allow gateway transit' enabled
The spoke address space must not overlap 192.168.0.0/16
exp: Gateway transit works when the hub allows it; a spoke using remote gateways can't have its own gateway; address spaces must not overlap.
